headline: Mistral AI's ARR hits $400M, targets $1B, with a $23B valuation
summary: The French AI decacorn, often misunderstood as an OpenAI competitor, focuses on deploying custom AI for governments and corporations, with an open-weight model coming this summer.
details: Mistral AI, the French AI company, has seen its annual recurring revenue (ARR) climb above $400 million, up from $20 million a year ago. The company is on track to surpass $1 billion in ARR this year and is rumored to be raising $3.5 billion at a $23.15 billion valuation.

Unlike direct competitors like OpenAI, Mistral AI follows a 'Palantir playbook,' deploying engineers to help governments and large corporations adopt and tailor AI for specific use cases. Its chat agent, Vibe, has less brand recognition than ChatGPT or Claude.

CEO Arthur Mensch clarified the company's core business involves deploying models and its agent platform on enterprise infrastructure, and building custom models with Forge. This strategy aims to provide secure and affordable AI technology as a commodity.

Mistral AI is committed to significant research investments to close the gap with foundational AI rivals. Mensch announced an exciting open-weight model set to arrive this summer, with early access opening in July.

To support its vision of building a 'true AI cloud,' Mistral AI recently acquired infrastructure startup Koyeb. The company also announced a €4 billion (approx. $4.56 billion) investment strategy for building data centers in France and Sweden.

Mistral's three founders, including CEO Arthur Mensch (ex-DeepMind) and CTO Timothée Lacroix and chief scientist Guillaume Lample (ex-Meta), bring strong AI research backgrounds from major U.S. tech companies.

headline_marked: [[n8n RAG pipelines leak PII]] to third-party LLMs, bypassing vector database security
headline: n8n RAG pipelines leak PII to third-party LLMs, bypassing vector database security
summary: RAG workflows in n8n often send sensitive internal document chunks as plain text to LLM providers like OpenAI, creating a critical data exposure risk.
details: While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is marketed for securely connecting corporate data to LLMs by keeping it in vector databases, a critical blind spot exists in n8n workflows. Many production n8n RAG pipelines inadvertently leak sensitive data.

The issue arises because retrieved document chunks, even from secure vector databases like Pinecone or Qdrant, are often shipped as plain text to third-party LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic). This exposes confidential financial reports, customer contracts, or HR policies.

This default behavior creates three major risks: direct PII exposure to LLM providers, data retention by these providers for up to 30 days (violating compliance frameworks like GDPR), and susceptibility to prompt injection attacks that can reveal internal context.

Common attempts to fix this within n8n, such as custom Code nodes with regex or n8n's built-in Guardrails node, only offer partial solutions. They often fail to cover the full spectrum of PII or are limited to explicitly defined patterns.

Privent addresses this by implementing reversible tokenization. It masks sensitive context before it reaches the LLM and then restores it before the user sees the answer, ensuring data privacy without disrupting the automation workflow.
caption:
